versions.changelog:
keyframe-animation 2.0.0

- **Requires ofox-video-core 2.0.0 or newer:** Billable subcommands now require `--approved`; core stops if missing or out of date.
- Add explicit compatibility requirement instructions.
- Update documentation to clarify approval flow and enforce cost confirmation before job submission.
- Remove deprecated "skill-card.md".
- Bump version and metadata to 2.0.0.

keyframe-animation 1.2.1

- Version bump: updates all references from 1.1.0 to 1.2.1.
- Broadened test base: describes a new, successful real-world test on a photographic subject with text, confirming both-ends lock and legibility.
- Major update to duration guidance: prior advice about easing now withdrawn; new measurement shows the interpolation curve depends on the input, not the model/tool.
- Documentation cleanup: removes redundant "skill-card.md" file.
- Keeps all requirements and usage the same; only tested claims, advice, and empirical results are updated.

keyframe-animation 1.1.0

- Updated to version 1.1.0 with metadata and documentation changes.
- SKILL.md version bumped; metadata now reflects v1.1.0.
- Minor improvements or clarifications to documentation.
- Removed the skill-card.md file, consolidating documentation.

keyframe-animation 1.0.1

- Bumped version to 1.0.1.
- SKILL.md: Updated measurement section — now based on two real runs with the same frame pair to confirm endpoint accuracy and prompt template function. Clarified which traits are tested and what is not claimed.
- SKILL.md: Updated version numbers in metadata.
- Removed redundant skill-card.md file.

keyframe-animation 1.0.0

- Initial release for two-image interpolation video generation via Ofox.
- Animates the motion between two user-supplied images (start and end frames) as a single video job.
- Relies on an existing OFOX_API_KEY and uses ofox-video-core for API and processing logic.
- Designed for "before/after" or "A to B" visual transitions; not for animating a single frame or UI state pairs.
- Includes guidance on usage, environmental setup, measured results, and supported scenarios.
